course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Data Processing (Hadoop and Spark)
course.description: This course introduces students to the principles, technologies, and applications of Big Data analytics. It covers the evolution of Big Data, its defining characteristics, and the role of advanced analytics in solving real-world problems. Students will explore key frameworks such as Hadoop, Spark, and Flink, along with concepts of real-time data processing, machine learning, and cloud-based solutions. The course emphasizes hands-on experience through labs and projects, including data stream processing, social media analytics, text mining, and sentiment analysis. Advanced topics such as deep learning architectures and parallelization strategies for distributed environments are also included. Learners will develop technical proficiency, analytical thinking, and ethical awareness while working collaboratively on projects. By the end of the course, students will be able to design and implement scalable Big Data solutions, apply machine learning techniques, and evaluate emerging technologies for data-driven decision-making.

contentRows: Topic 1: Introduction to Big Data and Historical Perspectives: Covers the evolution of Big Data and its significance.
Topic 2: Defining Big Data: From 3Vs to 32Vs: Explores the expanded definition of Big Data across domains.
Topic 3: Big Data Analytics and Machine Learning: Introduces ML concepts in the context of Big Data.
Topic 4: Big Data Analytics and Cloud Computing: Discusses cloud infrastructure for scalable analytics.
Topic 5: Hadoop, HDFS, MapReduce, Spark, and Flink: Overview of key Big Data processing frameworks.
Topic 6: Real-Time Analytics Concepts and Platforms: Covers velocity aspects and real-time data processing.
Topic 7: Data Stream Processing Platforms: Introduces tools like Spark Streaming, Storm, Kafka.
Topic 8: Big Data Analytics for Social Media: Applications of Big Data in analyzing social platforms.
Topic 9: Natural Language Processing and Applications: Language detection, named entity recognition, etc.
Topic 10: Text Mining and Sentiment Analysis: Techniques for extracting insights from text data.
Topic 11: Trending Topics and Recommender Systems: Algorithms for identifying trends and personalizing content.
Topic 12: Anomaly Detection in Social Media: Statistical and ML methods for detecting outliers.
Topic 13: Deep Learning Concepts and Architectures: Introduction to neural networks and deep learning.
Topic 14: Big Data Analytics for Social Media: Applications of Big Data in analyzing social platforms.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Big Data and Historical Perspectives: Covers the evolution of Big Data and its significance.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the evolution of Big Data and its role in modern analytics. LLO2: Identify key historical milestones that shaped Big Data technologies. LLO3: Discuss the significance of Big Data in real-world applications.

topics.title: Topic 2: Defining Big Data: From 3Vs to 32Vs: Explores the expanded definition of Big Data across domains.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define the original 3Vs and expanded Vs of Big Data. LLO2: Differentiate between various Vs and their impact on data processing. LLO3: Evaluate how additional Vs influence Big Data architecture design.

topics.title: Topic 3: Big Data Analytics and Machine Learning: Introduces ML concepts in the context of Big Data.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the relationship between Big Data and machine learning. LLO2: Apply ML algorithms to Big Data scenarios using sample datasets. LLO3: Analyze scalability challenges when integrating ML with Big Data.

topics.title: Topic 4: Big Data Analytics and Cloud Computing: Discusses cloud infrastructure for scalable analytics.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the role of cloud computing in Big Data analytics. LLO2: Compare different cloud-based Big Data platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP). LLO3: Deploy a simple Big Data pipeline on a cloud-like environment.

topics.title: Topic 5: Hadoop, HDFS, MapReduce, Spark, and Flink: Overview of key Big Data processing frameworks.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify the core components of Hadoop ecosystem. LLO2: Explain differences between MapReduce, Spark, and Flink frameworks. LLO3: Execute a basic Spark job for data processing.

topics.title: Topic 6: Real-Time Analytics Concepts and Platforms: Covers velocity aspects and real-time data processing.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define real-time analytics and its importance in Big Data. LLO2: Illustrate concepts like latency, windowing, and watermarking. LLO3: Implement a simple real-time data ingestion pipeline.

topics.title: Topic 7: Data Stream Processing Platforms: Introduces tools like Spark Streaming, Storm, Kafka.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the architecture of Spark Streaming, Storm, and Kafka. LLO2: Compare stream processing vs batch processing approaches. LLO3: Build a streaming pipeline using Spark Streaming and Kafka.

topics.title: Topic 8: Big Data Analytics for Social Media: Applications of Big Data in analyzing social platforms.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain how Big Data techniques apply to social media analytics. LLO2: Identify key metrics for social media engagement analysis. LLO3: Develop a pipeline for extracting insights from social media data.

topics.title: Topic 9: Natural Language Processing and Applications: Language detection, named entity recognition, etc.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: NLP concepts relevant to Big Data (tokenization, NER). LLO2: Apply NLP techniques for language detection in large datasets. LLO3: Analyze challenges of multilingual NLP in Big Data environments.

topics.title: Topic 10: Text Mining and Sentiment Analysis: Techniques for extracting insights from text data.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain text mining and its role in Big Data analytics. LLO2: Perform sentiment analysis on social media text streams. LLO3: Evaluate accuracy and scalability of sentiment models.

topics.title: Topic 11: Trending Topics and Recommender Systems: Algorithms for identifying trends and personalizing content.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe algorithms for detecting trending topics. LLO2: Implement a basic recommender system using Big Data tools. LLO3: Analyze personalization strategies in social media platforms.

topics.title: Topic 12: Anomaly Detection in Social Media: Statistical and ML methods for detecting outliers.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define anomaly detection and its significance in social media analytics. LLO2: Apply statistical and ML methods for detecting anomalies. LLO3: Evaluate performance of anomaly detection models on real datasets.

topics.title: Topic 13: Deep Learning Concepts and Architectures: Introduction to neural networks and deep learning.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain deep learning architectures for Big Data applications. LLO2: Implement a simple neural network for text classification. LLO3: Analyze parallelization strategies for training deep models at scale.

topics.title: Topic 14: Big Data Analytics for Social Media: Applications of Big Data in analyzing social platforms.
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Discuss ethical considerations in Big Data analytics. LLO2: Evaluate emerging trends in Big Data and AI integration. LLO3: Integrate course concepts into a capstone project design.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 1: Introduction to Big Data and Historical Perspectives: Covers the evolution of Big Data and its significance.
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture-Based Learning – Explain the evolution of Big Data and its role in modern analytics using slides and interactive discussion. LLO2: Project-Based Learning – Assign a mini-project where students research and present a timeline of Big Data milestones. LLO3: Lecture-Based Learning – Discuss the significance of Big Data in various domains through real-world examples.
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students take notes during lecture and summarize key historical milestones. LLO2: Students create a visual timeline (poster or infographic) and present findings. LLO3: Students analyze case studies and write a reflection on Big Data’s impact.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 2: Defining Big Data: From 3Vs to 32Vs: Explores the expanded definition of Big Data across domains.
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: LLO1: Lecture-Based Learning – Define the original 3Vs and expanded Vs of Big Data. LLO2: Group Discussion – Compare different Vs and their impact on data processing. LLO3: Case-Based Learning – Evaluate how additional Vs influence architecture design.
weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students list and explain Vs in their notebooks. LLO2: Students debate in groups and present findings on Vs importance. LLO3: Students analyze a case study and propose architecture adjustments.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 3: Big Data Analytics and Machine Learning: Introduces ML concepts in the context of Big Data.

weeks.activeLearningRaw: LLO1: Students answer concept questions during lecture. LLO2: Students implement a classifier on a sample dataset in lab. LLO3: Students write a short report on scalability issues.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 4: Big Data Analytics and Cloud Computing: Discusses cloud infrastructure for scalable analytics.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 6: Real-Time Analytics Concepts and Platforms: Covers velocity aspects and real-time data processing.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
